observation.visible_scene: A tattooed man in a grey long-sleeve shirt and black shorts stands on a sandy beach beside calm water and mangroves, with two green-and-white paddleboards resting near the shoreline behind him. He grips an orange resistance band with both hands; the band forms a taut horizontal segment between his hands and two vertical segments hanging down past his torso toward the ground.
visible_changes: From t=0 to about t=0.8s the man holds the band with his hands roughly at neck/chin height, the horizontal segment staying nearly static with only small shifts in hand position and head angle.

From roughly t=0.8s onward he presses his hands upward: the horizontal band segment rises from chin level (t=0.8–0.9s) to above his forehead and out toward the top of the frame (t=1.0s onward), and his arms extend from a bent position to nearly straight overhead.
His head tilts back and his gaze follows the band upward as the arms rise, then he holds the fully-extended overhead position with minor sway through the end of the clip (t=3.3s).

The framing tightens on his upper body over time: the paddleboards and waterline that fill the lower/right of the early frames progressively slide out of view toward the bottom, indicating an upward camera tilt and/or zoom rather than the man moving laterally.
Dark wet (sweat) patches on the front of his shirt become more pronounced around the chest/abdomen as the clip progresses, while his feet remain planted and his torso stays centered in the shot.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the band is anchored below his hands (the lower ends leave the frame; no anchor point is visible).
Whether the arms were already raised before t=0 or whether the overhead hold continues past t=3.3s; the segment ends mid-hold with no lowering or completion shown.
The purpose or full set structure of the exercise, which lies outside this excerpt.
uncertain_details: Whether the background shift is purely camera tilt, a zoom, or a combination; the man's own lateral position appears fixed.
Whether the increasing shirt wetness is sweat, water, or lighting variation cannot be confirmed from the frames alone.
Small hand-grip and band-tension changes between frames are within normal holding jitter and not clearly a deliberate motion.
